title: Error/empty/loading states, mobile pass, dark mode
goal: Close REQ-26's polish gap: every one of this app's 13 page routes currently has zero App Router error.tsx/loading.tsx/not-found.tsx boundaries (confirmed by directory listing -- none exist anywhere in app/), so an unhandled Server Component throw or slow data fetch renders Next's generic unstyled crash screen or a blank page instead of anything on-brand. Dark mode CSS variables already exist (app/globals.css's .dark block) but nothing in the app ever applies the .dark class, and ~13 call sites use fixed light-tuned Tailwind color utilities (text-red-600, bg-yellow-100, etc.) that won't read correctly once dark mode is live.
in_scope: app/error.tsx (segment error boundary, 'use client', receives {error, reset}) and app/global-error.tsx (root-level fallback -- must render its own <html>/<body> per Next's convention since it replaces the root layout on catastrophic failure) -- both styled with the existing Card components, a plain-language message, and a reset/retry action.
app/not-found.tsx -- styled 404 for any unmatched route, using the same Card/Link pattern as every other page's outbound links.

app/loading.tsx (root-level Suspense fallback) -- a single shared loading state, not 13 duplicated ones: Next applies the nearest loading.tsx up the route tree to every segment beneath it that doesn't define its own, which is exactly the 'every screen defines a loading state' requirement without hand-duplicating the same skeleton 13 times. A route gets its own loading.tsx only if this audit finds its loading needs are actually distinct (none currently do -- all 13 pages are single force-dynamic RSC fetches with no nested Suspense boundaries).

Empty-state audit across all 13 routes (Today, Inventory, Plan, Shopping List, Insights, Catalog, Review queue, Review detail, Add, Add manual, Settings, Onboarding, Inventory detail): confirm each already has a defined zero-data render (several do -- Inventory's 'No items match these filters', Today's cold-start copy per A13) and add one to whichever genuinely lacks it, found by reading each page's data-fetch + render path, not assumed.

Mobile-viewport pass: code-trace review of every page/component for horizontal-overflow risk (fixed-width inline styles, non-wrapping flex rows, form controls without width constraints) and touch-target sizing on interactive elements (buttons, checkboxes) below the ~44px comfortable-tap guideline. Fixed where genuinely found, not a blanket rewrite -- most pages already use flex-wrap and the shadcn Button/Checkbox primitives, which are reasonably sized by default.

Dark mode, part 1 -- making it functional at all: an inline, render-blocking script in app/layout.tsx's <head> (runs before hydration, avoiding a light->dark flash) that reads `matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)')`, applies/removes the `.dark` class on <html> accordingly, and listens for live OS-theme changes. No manual light/dark toggle UI is added -- the acceptance criterion is 'dark mode functional', not 'a theme switcher exists', and this app has no settings surface for display preferences today.

Dark mode, part 2 -- fixing the ~13 call sites (found via grep across app/ for text-/bg-/border- + red|green|blue|yellow|amber|gray|slate|zinc|neutral|orange + a Tailwind shade number) that use fixed light-tuned palette shades for status color (errors, success confirmations, warning banners, info callouts) in app/insights/page.tsx, app/settings/{settings-form,page,data-tools-panel}.tsx, app/review/[id]/review-detail.tsx, app/add/capture.tsx, app/add/manual/manual-entry-form.tsx: add `dark:` variant overrides so each remains legible (sufficient contrast, not muddy) against the dark background token, verified by reading the resulting computed class list against both --background values, not by an actual rendered screenshot (no headless browser in this repo).
out_of_scope: Per-route loading.tsx duplication where the shared root one already covers the case -- adding 13 near-identical files would be the abstraction-beyond-what's-needed anti-pattern this repo's conventions explicitly avoid.
A user-facing theme toggle / persisted preference -- system-preference-driven only, per this story's acceptance wording ('functional', not 'user-controllable'). Revisit only if a real user ever asks.

Any component library swap or design-token restructuring -- the semantic tokens (bg-background, text-foreground, etc.) already flow correctly through .dark; this story only fixes the small set of call sites that bypassed them with fixed palette shades.

Full Lighthouse/axe accessibility audit beyond touch-target sizing and color contrast incidental to the dark-mode fix -- REQ-26's acceptance criterion is about error/empty/loading/mobile/dark-mode, not a general a11y pass.
acceptance: Every screen defines an error, empty, and loading state (no blank/broken renders); full mobile-viewport pass; dark mode functional across the app.
invariants: app/global-error.tsx renders a complete, valid <html>/<body> document -- it replaces the root layout entirely on the failure path it handles, unlike every other error/not-found boundary in this app.
The dark-mode-detection script runs synchronously before first paint (blocking <head> script, not a useEffect) -- a flash of the wrong theme on load is the exact bug this pattern exists to prevent.

No empty-state or loading-state addition changes any page's force-dynamic data-fetching behavior or introduces a new client-side data fetch -- these are presentation-only additions over the existing Server Component fetch pattern.
